title: Where is bondage?
hookLine: the last chapter is one small word asked over and over: where?
tomorrow: Why did the breath get up to leave?

cards: Kva. In Sanskrit it means where. It's a small word, the kind a child uses looking for a lost shoe.
And the last chapter of the Ashtavakra Gita is built almost entirely out of it. Verse after verse, Janaka asks where. Not where is my kingdom, or where did I leave the keys.
He asks where the things are that this path spends so long seeking. By the end, the word has asked about nearly everything, and the book simply stops.

teach.h: WHERE IS THE BODY, THE MIND, SCRIPTURE?
teach.b: Here's the shape of it, in paraphrase. Where are the elements, Janaka asks, where is the body, the senses, the mind, for me, spotless by nature? Where is scripture?
Where is knowledge of the Self?

teach.h: WHERE IS BONDAGE? WHERE IS LIBERATION?
teach.b: Then the line that stops a reader short: where is bondage, and where is liberation?
A verse later: where is the karma already begun, where is freedom while living? Janaka asked about freedom on the first page; the sage told him he was free if he took himself as free.
Now, at the end, the student isn't celebrating his freedom. For what he is, even bound and free have nowhere to stand. That's why it's a where and not a no.
He isn't saying scripture is wrong or liberation a myth. He looks for them in awareness itself, and finds nothing there that needs them.

teach.h: MOKSHA: THE SELF WAS NEVER BOUND.
teach.b: That's Advaita's teaching on moksha, liberation, at its starkest: freedom isn't a prize you win, because the Self was never bound. On this reading, the medicine has done its work, and the bottle can go back on the shelf.
The whole book in a breath: a king asks how to be free, a sage says he already is, and the king's last word is where. It also closes this year's lineage track, three roads Hindus have long named.
Karma, the road of action: the Gita's chapters on action, and a year of service designed. Bhakti, the road of devotion: the Gita Govinda, the Bhagavata's tenth book, kirtan.
Jnana, the road of knowing: the Vivekachudamani and this book. Plenty of Hindu families walk more than one at once, a puja in the morning, work offered by day, a page of scripture at night.
None is asked to stand in for the others.

how: The Ashtavakra Gita ends with Janaka's chapter of questions beginning with kva, where; some students reread it slowly at the close of their study, asking each where for themselves.

s: the last chapter of the Ashtavakra Gita ends in a big celebration of liberation
Janaka asks where even bondage and liberation are, for what he is.
Janaka's where means scripture and liberation are false
it's a where, not a no: he looks for them in awareness and finds nothing that needs them.
in the last chapter, Janaka asks where even bondage and liberation are
on the Advaita reading, the Self was never bound, so neither word has anywhere to stand.

games.q: you're Janaka at the end of the book. the sage has said everything. what is your last word?
o: thank you, I am free now.
games.why: the last chapter asks where, verse after verse, even of bondage and liberation.

practice: Borrow Janaka's small word and ask it gently, without hunting for answers. Where is the body? Where is the mind?
Where is the one who is trying to be free? After each where, rest in the quiet the question leaves.
